items.prompt:
Two articles about one game: one praises the winners, one blames the losers. They differ in:
A) point of view/focus
B) the sport
C) the date

Both accounts of a flood say the river overflowed. This is a:
A) similarity
B) difference
C) opinion

Reading more than one account of an event helps you get:
A) a fuller, more balanced understanding
B) fewer facts
C) confused on purpose
items.answer: A) a fuller, more balanced understanding

steps: Multiple views = balance. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) a fuller, more balanced understanding

items.prompt:
A writer who includes only facts that favor one side is showing a:
A) balanced view
B) biased point of view
C) complete view

Two eyewitness accounts of a car crash give different details. This shows that accounts can:
A) always match exactly
B) differ based on each person's point of view
C) never be trusted at all
items.answer: B) differ based on each person's point of view

solution.answer: B) differ based on each person's point of view

items.prompt:
To analyze two accounts well, you should note their:
A) similarities and differences
B) page counts only
C) fonts

Account A of a protest stresses peaceful marchers; Account B stresses a few broken windows. A careful reader concludes:
A) only A is true
B) each account emphasizes different facts, so reading both gives a fuller picture
C) protests never happen
items.answer: B) each account emphasizes different facts, so reading both gives a fuller picture

solution.answer: B) each account emphasizes different facts, so reading both gives a fuller picture

items.prompt:
Why might two writers describe the SAME event so differently?
A) Their points of view lead them to emphasize different facts and opinions
B) One writer is always lying
C) Events have no facts
items.answer: A) Their points of view lead them to emphasize different facts and opinions

steps: Point of view shapes accounts. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) Their points of view lead them to emphasize different facts and opinions
